Guidance & outlook: According to the IMF's April 2026 World Economic Outlook, global GDP growth is projected at 3.1% in 2026, reflecting the impact of higher commodity prices, disrupted shipping routes, and cautious business sentiment.

Population growth toward 9.1 Bn, pest-driven yield losses of 20-40%, and climate-induced pest migration are emerging as key demand drivers, reinforcing the need for food security and accelerating the adoption of digital tools across modern farming systems, which is expected to sustain sectoral growth.
OPERATIONAL PERFORMANCE & FUTURE OUTLOOK: The Company's consolidated revenue from operations increased by 21.94% on YoY basis from ` 4,31,985.30 Lakhs to ` 5,26,758.52 Lakhs in 2025-26.
Growth & demand: The strength of this approach was reflected in 2025-26, with revenue growing by 22%, supported by volume-led growth and improved profitability as costs stabilised and operating leverage strengthened.
Real GDP grew by 7.4% in 2025-26, while growth for 2026-27 is projected in the range of 6.8%-7.2%, reflecting strong medium-term economic momentum despite global uncertainties.

Key growth drivers include population growth toward 9.7 Bn by 2050, drone-based application reducing chemical volumes by 10-20%, and over 500 resistant weed biotypes compelling more intensive herbicide programmes.
Margins & costs: Revenue crossed the ` 5,000 Cr. mark for the first time, while EBITDA and Profit After Tax reached record highs.
Gross margins expanded by approximately 600 basis points to 35.9%, reflecting healthier industry conditions, sourcing efficiencies, product mix improvements, and disciplined cost management.
Volatility in energy and commodity markets has increased input and logistics costs across industries, creating renewed inflationary pressures after the disinflation progress achieved in 2025.
Capex & expansion: This has prompted a broader shift across the industry towards disciplined capital allocation, focused on productivity enhancement, debottlenecking and supply-chain optimisation rather than aggressive capacity expansion.
7.4% Real GDP Growth Recorded during 2025-26 6.8-7.2% Projected GDP Growth for 2026-27 [Source: Economic Survey 2025-26] Sectoral performance underscores this balanced expansion.

The government continues to anchor stability through credible fiscal consolidation, aiming to contain the fiscal deficit below 4.5% of GDP , alongside a sustained push in effective capital expenditure, which has structurally risen to around 4% of GDP .
Balance sheet & cash: We remained debt-free throughout the year and ended the period with ` 702 Cr. in cash and liquid investments.
Net worth increased to ` 3,137 Cr. while disciplined working capital management reduced the working capital cycle to 98 days.
The aggregate gross amount of Interim Dividend Distributed is ` 5,413.23 Lakhs subject to TDS as applicable.
